title: Qazi’s Counsel and the Public Dragging of Banda Singh’s Body

blocks.text: After the capture, Farrukhsiar kept Banda blind for many days while the court weighed how much cruelty was still owed to so famous an enemy. The debate is not framed as mercy but as calculation, with hostile courtiers insisting that sparing him would only magnify imperial weakness.

A qazi identified with Wazir Khan's family pressed the harshest line and warned that the emperor would regret sparing Banda. His counsel was that Banda should be killed and then dragged behind a horse through the city of Delhi so that punishment itself became a public spectacle.

The page therefore records the move from captivity to exemplary vengeance. What had been a military victory was now turned into a juridical and theatrical performance meant to satisfy revenge as much as state power.
